answers.transcript:
Okay, so I want to talk about my grandfather, he is the father of my father.
He is eighty-two years old and he live alone in a small village.
We visit him in every summer holiday and we speak in the telephone every Sunday.
My mother calls him first and after that she gives the phone to me.
He always talks about the old times, when he was a young man in the army.
He tell me the same stories many times but I don't say nothing, I only listen.
For example, in his village before there was no electricity and the people go to the town with a horse.
Sometimes he talk about my grandmother also, she is died five years ago.
I enjoy to listen him because his life is very very different from my life.
In my opinion the young people can learn many thing from this stories.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: All four points on the card are touched on and the talk does not break off, but each point is skimmed in a single sentence and links never go beyond the and / because / also / for example pattern. The section on what the grandfather talks about closes after two sentences, and the example is left unopened.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Vocabulary stays in the everyday core: old times, stories, listen, different repeat, and emphasis is made with "very very different". There is not a single collocation or idiom that describes listening to an elderly person.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Agreement, tense or preposition errors are spread across most sentences (he live, he tell, he talk, the people go, in the telephone, she is died, many thing, this stories), but meaning is never closed off. Structures are simple; there is no complex structure beyond the two clauses built with when and because.

answers.what_would_lift_it: First, open up one of the things the grandfather talks about as a real scene — which story, where, what happened — because at present topics are only listed as headings. Then fix agreement errors of the "he live / he tell / he talk" kind, since they repeat in every sentence.

answers.transcript:
So the person I'm going to talk about is my grandfather, my father's father, and he's, er, eighty-two now.
He lives alone in a small village in the Black Sea region, so we can only visit him in the summer, but we speak on the phone every Sunday evening.
Usually my mother calls him first and then she gives the phone to me, and we make a long conversation, maybe twenty minutes.
The thing he talks about the most is his memories from the past, especially the years of his military service.
He tells the same stories many times, I have to be honest, but somehow I don't get bored from them.
For example, he describes his village before the electricity came, when people were going to town by horse, and for me it's like another century.
Sometimes he talks about my grandmother also, she passed away five years ago, and in these moments he becomes quiet.
The reason I enjoy listening him is that his life was completely different from mine.
When I have a problem, he never gives me an advice directly, he just tells one story and I understand the point by myself.
I think this is very valuable, and, er, that's why I like our Sunday conversations.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: All four points are developed and the transition between the phone scene and the village example feels natural. On the other hand, section openings repeat in the pattern "Usually", "For example", "Sometimes", "The reason", and the narrative stops at one point and turns into a list.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: There is enough vocabulary to carry the topic (military service, passed away, memories, valuable) and meaning is clear throughout. Collocation slips in two places: "we make a long conversation", "I don't get bored from them".
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: A relative clause, the past continuous, a time clause and a noun clause built with "the reason" are controlled; more than two-thirds of sentences are error-free. The remaining errors sit in a narrow set: dropped prepositions (enjoy listening him), an article with an uncountable noun (an advice), "get bored from".

answers.what_would_lift_it: Tell one of the grandfather's stories from start to finish: at present it is said that "he always describes his village", but a single story itself never actually arrives. Fixing isolated errors such as "listening him" and "an advice" in the language is enough; the rest of the structure is already solid.

answers.transcript:
So, the person I'd pick is my grandfather, my dad's father, who's eighty-two and still living on his own in a village up on the Black Sea coast.
We only get up there in the summer, but we ring him most Sunday evenings, and my mum always hands the phone over to me after about five minutes, so I've probably spoken to him more than anyone else in the family has.
He's absolutely full of stories, that's the thing.
Nine times out of ten it's his military service, or, well, the village the way it was before the road went in. No electricity, everyone going into town on horseback, which to me sounds like a completely different world.
And yes, I've heard most of them before, but he has this way of putting things that means you don't really mind. He'll drop in some tiny detail he's never mentioned, and suddenly the whole story lands differently.
He talks about my grandmother as well. She died about five years ago, and he goes very quiet afterwards, so I've learnt to let the silence sit there rather than filling it.
As for why I enjoy it, I think it's that it puts things in perspective.
If I'm panicking about my exams, he'll never tell me straight out what to do. He just tells me something that happened to him in 1962 and leaves me to work out the connection myself, which sounds a bit roundabout, but it works every time.

why_this_band.fluency_coherence: The narrative builds its own order and sections connect on their own ("He's absolutely full of stories, that's the thing", "As for why I enjoy it"). There is one self-correction ("or, well, the village the way it was"), the rare kind of correction that eight lines allow.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Less common items are plentiful and exactly in place: full of stories, nine times out of ten, has this way of putting things, a completely different world, on horseback, puts things in perspective, tell me straight out, work out the connection, a bit roundabout. The register is spoken throughout.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Structural range is wide: relative clauses, the present perfect (I've probably spoken to him more than anyone else in the family has), a conditional clause, the "leaves me to work out" pattern. There is no countable error, and the accuracy never stops the listener anywhere.

answers.what_would_lift_it: This is on target; for the next level up, the lesson drawn from what the grandfather says needs to be closed with a single concrete example of what it touches today — at present the 1962 reference is left without an example. There is nothing left to do in the language.
